passage:
Before Moon Festival, Class 805 prepared gift boxes for elderly people who lived alone. Each box had fruit, tea, moon cakes, and a handmade card.
Some students wanted to write long messages. Others did not know what to say. Their teacher told them simple words were enough if they were honest.
When the boxes were delivered, one old man read his card three times. It said, "We hope you have a warm evening."
The students realized that the card mattered as much as the food.
A festival is often about family, but not everyone has family nearby. The boxes could not solve loneliness, but they could carry a message: someone remembered you today.
